label: New baby in the family

what_happens.title: What happens when the baby comes
goals: When the baby is born, some grown-ups go to the hospital for a few days
The child stays with a grown-up they know, then meets the baby
Then the baby comes home, and the family has a new rhythm
what_happens.parentSkill: Tell your child exactly who will look after them and where they will sleep.

who_is_there.title: Who is in my family now
goals: The child is still the same special big sibling
A trusted helper looks after the child; nurses help at the hospital
A new baby is tiny, sleeps a lot and cries to talk
who_is_there.parentSkill: Show photos of the child as a baby and tell the story of their own first days.

what_i_do.title: What I can do as a big sibling
goals: Big-sibling jobs: bring a diaper, sing a song, choose a sock
Gentle hands and quiet voices around the baby
My own toys can stay mine, and I choose what to share
what_i_do.parentSkill: Give your child one real job and thank them for it every time.

if_scared.title: If I feel worried or cross
goals: Missing grown-ups, feeling cross or jealous are all okay
Love does not get smaller when the family gets bigger
Special one-on-one time is still there
if_scared.parentSkill: Welcome big feelings: 'You wish it was just us sometimes. That's okay to feel.'

rehearsal.title: Let's practise being a big sibling
goals: Practise holding a doll gently and singing to it
Walk through the days: helper, meeting the baby, coming home
Celebrate the child as a big sibling
rehearsal.parentSkill: Practise with a doll and let your child show you how gentle hands look.

steps: A trusted grown-up comes to stay with the child
Some grown-ups go to the hospital when the baby is ready to be born
The child visits or waits at home and talks on the phone
The child meets the baby, maybe with a gift from the baby
The baby comes home and sleeps, eats and cries a lot
The child keeps special one-on-one time with a grown-up
The child helps with a small job, like choosing the baby's socks
sensory: a tiny baby that smells of milk and soap
a baby's cry that can be loud
a quiet house while the baby sleeps
the beeps and long halls of a hospital
tiny clothes and a small bath
honestyNotes: A baby cries, needs a lot of care and takes grown-ups' time. Never promise nothing will change. Promise what is true: the child is loved the same and has special time, and grown-ups come back from the hospital.

fallbackAnswer: Yes. Love does not get smaller when a family gets bigger.
You are still [[GROWNUP]]'s special one, and you always will be.

questionButtons.text: Will my toys be given away?
fallbackAnswer: You can choose if you want to share something with the baby, when you are ready.

questionButtons.text: Where will I be when the baby is born?
fallbackAnswer: You will stay with a grown-up you know, and you will be looked after.
The grown-ups come back from the hospital, and you will meet the baby soon.

questionButtons.text: Why do babies cry so much?
fallbackAnswer: Babies can't talk yet, so crying is how they say 'I'm hungry' or 'I'm tired'.
When it gets loud, you can cover your ears or go to a quiet spot.
Yes, when you sit down and a grown-up helps you.
Babies need gentle hands, and you can practise with a doll.

questionButtons.text: What happens when the baby comes?
fallbackAnswer: First you stay with a helper you know, then you meet the baby.
After that, the baby comes home, and you become a big sibling.

questionButtons.text: When can the baby play with me?
fallbackAnswer: New babies mostly sleep, eat and cry.
In a few months the baby will smile at you, and later you can play together.

questionButtons.text: Who looks after me when the baby is born?
fallbackAnswer: [[GROWNUP]] will tell you who looks after you while the baby is born.
It will be someone you know and like.

questionButtons.text: Why does the baby need so much help?
fallbackAnswer: Babies cannot walk, talk or eat by themselves yet.
Grown-ups help them, just like they helped you when you were tiny.

techniques.label: A big-sibling job
techniques.how: Give one real job, like bringing a diaper or choosing the baby's socks, and thank your child each time.

techniques.label: Special one-on-one time
techniques.how: Keep ten minutes a day only for your older child, without the baby, and call it by a name.

techniques.label: A gift from the baby
techniques.how: Have a small gift 'from the baby' ready for the first meeting.

techniques.label: A clear helper plan
techniques.how: Tell your child who will look after them, where they will sleep, and practise a phone call.

techniques.label: Gentle hands with a doll
techniques.how: Practise holding a doll with support under the head, and stroking gently.

techniques.label: A quiet spot for loud moments
techniques.how: Make a cosy spot with books where your child can go when the baby cries.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

techniques.label: Looking at my baby photos
techniques.how: Look at photos of your child as a baby and tell how you cared for them.

techniques.label: Naming big feelings
techniques.how: Say feelings out loud for your child: 'You wish the baby would go back. That's a big feeling, and I love you.'
